conditioningLevel.rationale: Exactly one §9.1 structural signal is satisfied. The credited segment is six entries long and contains one cationic, one fatty alcohol, one amphoteric surfactant, one glycol and one silicone — no lipid at all. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.

COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE (rank 3) — an AMPHOTERIC surfactant, deliberately NOT counted toward S1; it is a cleansing/foam agent, not a long-chain cationic quat or protonatable amidoamine
CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 25) — a second cationic, deep in the tail

`high` does not apply: only S2 holds.

`low` does not apply: Cetearyl Alcohol @2 defeats its second conjunct. Note that on substance this formula is the leanest conventional emulsion in the cohort and `low` would arguably describe it better — a further instance of AP-07-LOWUNREACHABLE, here on the conditioning scale rather than the weight scale.

Confidence `moderate` and additionally capped by the fired `tail_marker_anomaly`: only one signal is available, the source is retailer-aggregated rather than verbatim, and the marker's plausibility is contested.

Re-derived under v0.2 (R8 marker move, R3): the value `moderate` STANDS on the enlarged credited segment (ranks 1–11 against HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, not ranks 1–6 against the colourant @7). S1 fails — BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 is the only cationic surfactant above the tail; COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE @3 is amphoteric and is not a cationic conditioning agent, and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @25 is deep in the tail. S2 is satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2. S3 fails: COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 is the only non-fatty-alcohol lipid above the tail, and one is not breadth. One signal; S1 absent. The tail-edge exclusion removes HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR @11, which carries no structural signal in any case. No material counter-signal fires — and note that the v0.1 reviewer-judgment `tail_marker_anomaly` that capped this field is withdrawn, since R8 resolves the colourant question by rule.

Re-derived under v0.3 (E2). The VALUE `moderate` stands, now on two independent grounds. (1) On the ordinal read, S1 still fails: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 is the only cationic surfactant in the head, COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE @3 is amphoteric and is not an S1 species, and S3 fails for want of any established above-tail lipid breadth. (2) Independently, §9.1's MATERIAL COUNTER-SIGNAL (a) now FIRES — `tail_marker` is `unresolved` — which caps `conditioning_level` at `moderate` whatever the signal count, and lists the field in `uncertain_fields`. Recorded so the competing reading is visible: on a PARFUM @30 marker, CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @25 would be above the tail, S1 would fire on two cationics, and the field would read `high`. That reading is exactly what counter-signal (a) exists to refuse — the segment the signals would be counted on is not reliable — so `moderate` is the value under both the ordinal read and the cap. Confidence `moderate` under §9.1's confidence rule (mandatory when the marker is `absent`/`unresolved`).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.
Formula source is aggregated across three retailer listings, not a single verbatim page; the cohort capture itself recommends a direct re-fetch at freeze time.

weightPotential.rationale: Re-derived under v0.3 (E2). REVERTED from v0.2's `high` to `moderate`. v0.2's `high` rested entirely on COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 being above the tail, which was true only because it outranks HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12. With the marker `unresolved`, §3.1.1 clause 2 forbids exactly that: nothing may be credited as above-tail architecture SOLELY because it outranks an implausible marker. The `high` anchor therefore has no established heavy-lipid core and does not clear. `low` is independently unavailable — §9.2 states that the leanness test cannot run on an unreadable segment — so `moderate` is the residual the rule prescribes, listed in `uncertain_fields` and routed to review. This is not a finding that the product is mid-weight; it is the conservative NEQI value for a formula whose boundary cannot be read. Both readings are recorded below. E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.
evidenceSignals: tail_marker = UNRESOLVED (HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, a declared allergen, against PARFUM @30 — §3.1.1 third limb, E2). Every rank-relative credit on this record is therefore provisional

COCOS NUCIFERA OIL/COCONUT OIL (rank 9) — §5 names it among the R4b heavy triglycerides, so it WOULD be the `high` anchor's required core if it were established as above-tail. Its above-tail status rests solely on outranking the unresolved marker, so §3.1.1 clause 2 forbids crediting it. It is recorded as an E1 formula fact and earns nothing
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — cetearyl-class fatty alcohol within the top three ranks: completer (a) is available and is NOT the problem. The anchor fails on its required core, not on its completer

AMODIMETHICONE (rank 6) — a single silicone species; completer (b), the occlusive silicone stack, needs two silicone species or a dimethicone/dimethiconol pair and is unavailable under any marker reading

BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) — the only cationic surfactant in the credited head; CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @25 sits far down the list. Recorded for the `low` test's third conjunct, which is not reached
PROPYLENE GLYCOL DICAPRYLATE/DICAPRATE (rank 21) — a light ester, credited nowhere under any reading
weightPotential.derivation: §9.2 under §3.1.1's unresolved-marker consequences. `high` requires an R4b heavy lipid ESTABLISHED above the marker; COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9's above-tail status is exactly what the unresolved marker cannot establish (clause 2), so the required core is absent and `high` fails. `low` is unavailable by §9.2's own rule — the positive leanness test may not run on an unreadable segment, and the field takes `moderate` and goes to `uncertain_fields`. Residual and prescribed value = `moderate`. Note the two conjuncts of E4's new leanness test that CAN be checked would both hold (no occlusive silicone stack; a single cationic species in the head) — which is recorded only to show that `low` is refused on marker readability, not on architecture.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: the residual, and the value §9.2 explicitly prescribes when the above-tail segment is not readable. It goes to `uncertain_fields` with it.

`high` does not apply under v0.3: its required heavy-lipid core cannot be established. §3.1.1 clause 2 is directional and binding — an implausible marker never pushes a value UP, and crediting COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 as above-tail architecture purely on the strength of outranking @12 is precisely that.

`low` does not apply: not because the architecture is rich, but because §9.2 makes the leanness test unavailable on an unresolved marker. §1.1 governs — an absence-based `low` would hand a lean fit prior, and therefore a fine-hair recommendation, to a product we could not read.

THE COMPETING READING, RECORDED (§3.1.1 clause 5 — `unresolved` is a review state, never a shortcut in either direction): if the marker were taken at PARFUM @30, COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 would be above the tail, the R4b core would be established, CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 would complete it, and `weight_potential` would be `high` (`rich`). That is v0.2's recorded value. The two readings differ by one species at one rank and produce the category's mildest and richest weight priors respectively. Neither is auto-selected; the conservative one is recorded and the pair is escalated in AP-11-MARKERUNRESOLVED.

§9.2 conflict fallback not engaged separately: no `high` was reached, so `weight_high_conflict` has nothing to fire on. The tension a five-minute gloss treatment would create with a `rich` prior is recorded in the adjudication point rather than as a trigger.
limitations: Weight drives a soft preference with a stated reason, never an exclusion; fine-hair flattening is a fit mismatch, not a hair-type law (§9.2 wording rule).
An ingredient-informed matching prior at E2, never a prediction that the product will visibly flatten hair.
Both readings on record (§3.1.1 clause 5): `moderate` on the conservative unresolved-marker reading recorded here; `high`/`rich` on the resolved-marker reading. See the adjudication point.

E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.

`protein` does not apply: no protein exists anywhere. (D6 notes the sibling case Balea Glow & Shine reaches `protein` because its keratin route is material; this product has no such route.)
`balanced` does not apply: its first conjunct is the material R5 route.
Confidence `moderate` rather than `high`: the route separation is unambiguous, but the fired `tail_marker_anomaly` and the aggregated source cap it.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R6, on the re-derived segment). `moisture` STANDS. Reading (a) is unavailable (no R5 species at any rank). Reading (b) — the film-/acid-led `neither_dominant` read whose named anchor case in §9.3 is THIS PRODUCT — is tested in full and FAILS at clause 4. Clause 1 holds (no protein anchor). Clause 2 holds (AMODIMETHICONE @6 is a substantive R2 silicone above the tail, and GLYCOLIC ACID @29 is the R6a acid whose positioning carries the product). Clause 3 holds (one humectant-class species, PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5, is not a pair; and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 alone does not satisfy S3, so there is no lipid stack). Clause 4 FAILS: it requires every film/acid species establishing clause 2 to rank ABOVE every candidate leg species noted under clause 3, and AMODIMETHICONE @6 sits one rank BELOW PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5. The reading is therefore refused on a single rank. This is a direct answer to §18 open question 6 and is escalated with AP-11-COCONUT: the standard names this product as reading (b)'s anchor case, and on its real INCI the clause the standard added to keep the read honest is exactly what blocks it.

Re-checked under v0.3 (E2). `moisture` STANDS, and the reasoning is unchanged in substance: there is no protein species at any rank under any marker reading, so `protein` and `balanced` reading (a) are closed absolutely; reading (b) fails at clause 4 because AMODIMETHICONE @6 sits one rank BELOW PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5. §9.3's confidence rule for reading (b) would step a record to `low` where the leg-absence read rests on an `absent`/`unresolved` marker — but reading (b) is not taken here, and `moisture` does not rest on the marker at all: it rests on the total absence of protein, which no marker reading changes. Confidence stays `moderate`, capped by the unresolved marker per §9.3's confidence rule, not stepped to `low`.
limitations: Banned wording observed absolutely — see the shine record.

focus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation plus one M3 optical observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 at any rank, no bond token; R6a can never set repair); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic in the head, no established above-tail polymer); `color_care` blocked (the CI entries are the product's own dye load, and colour-DEPOSITING masks are excluded at G0 in any case); `lightness` blocked (weight_potential is `moderate`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at §9.5.3 criterion 1 (PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 is the only humectant-class species with a secure position, against a required three). Step 5 `shine`: criterion 1 holds — the optical architecture is present and no R4b heavy lipid is established above the tail; criterion 2 holds — the amino silicone is a distinct addition to an unusually thin base, not the base's own film; criterion 3 holds on exact-product positioning, used as corroboration only. Selected. Secondary: §6 rule 2 and the §9.5.2 secondary rule: a secondary must add useful matching information rather than restate the primary's mechanism. §9.5.3 criterion 1 fails for moisture.
thresholdReasoning: Criterion 1 CLEARS: an alignment-oriented R2 silicone above the tail with a comparatively low lipid load and no R4b heavy lipid established above the tail. The condition is met because §3.1.1 clause 2 withholds the coconut oil's above-tail credit — not because the species is absent. That distinction is stated plainly because it is the whole of the difference from v0.2.

Criterion 2 CLEARS: the optical route is not merely a smoothing film already counted. No smoothing focus was awarded, and the architecture is not the ordinary M1 deposition — a thin base with one alignment-oriented amino silicone is the shape §9.5.4 describes as distinguishing a gloss product from a rich nourishing mask.

Criterion 3 CLEARS on claim corroboration — the one legitimately claim-gated leg in this record. Gloss, Glaze, Laminierung and Glanz positioning are all present in the exact-product name and claims. Corroboration only: it could not have created the route, and criteria 1 and 2 were established blind.
